claims.statement: The official payment workflow can require invoices, proof of payment, product cards, technical evidence, an energy audit summary, and other attachments depending on project scope.

NFOŚiGW updated operator checklists for rules effective 20 July 2026 and clarified that the final-visit protocol is not itself definitive proof of correct grant execution, demonstrating document-version and evidence complexity.

Hypothesis: invoice and photo checks performed before customer handover can remove enough rework to support a 600 to 1,200 PLN per-project price; contractor interviews and rejected-pack data are still required.

contrary_evidence: Beneficiaries can receive free assistance from municipal consultation points and program operators, which may suppress willingness to pay for another checker.
Many contractors may handle too few eligible jobs for a subscription and may pass responsibility to the beneficiary or auditor.

economics.acquisition_route: Validate on family-company jobs, then let auditors and wholesalers bundle the pack at project close
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 30 contractors and 600 packs produce about 0.5M PLN revenue in year 1; 250 contractors and 6,000 packs can exceed 5M PLN revenue by year 4. At 1.5M PLN EBITDA, a 4x value and 70% ownership imply 4.2M PLN equity; retained reinvested cash must add roughly 0.8M PLN for a 5M PLN net-worth path in years 6 to 7.
economics.founder_time: 10 to 15 hours weekly during the first 100 dossiers, falling as exception rules stabilize
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70% to 85% after OCR and deterministic checks; human review is limited to flagged exceptions
economics.payback: One avoided callback, invoice correction, or delayed payment should cover a pack; measure actual hours and cash delay in the first 50 jobs
economics.pricing: 600 to 1,200 PLN per completed job plus 499 PLN monthly for rule alerts and team workflow
economics.retention_or_repeat: Contractors repeat per installation, while changing forms and audit retention needs support subscription renewal

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A region-and-program-version defect corpus showing which evidence omissions cause questions, corrections, or delays
fingerprint.customer: Small Polish heat-pump, insulation, and retrofit contractors completing Czyste Powietrze projects
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Family-company proof, energy auditors, equipment wholesalers, and municipal-operator training partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Per-project evidence gate plus a lightweight monthly contractor workspace
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The contractor pays when a job is checked and exported, or when renewing rule-version monitoring
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Installation is nearing acceptance and the contractor needs a complete customer payment and audit dossier

founder_fit: The family company offers direct workflow access and a low-cost Wielkopolska pilot, while document parsing and rules engines match the founder's AI and data skills. The initial service can run asynchronously and part-time, then productize rather than becoming manual grant consultancy.
risks: Customers may mistake automated checks for grant eligibility or legal certification.
The workflow contains identity, property, invoice, and financial data requiring GDPR controls.
Program rule changes could strand templates or sharply reduce project volume.

structure.control_point: The evidence pack assembled immediately before final customer and grant payment submission
structure.critical_dependency: Contractors must experience measurable payment delay or rework that the checker can prevent

thesis: Offer a per-job pre-submission gate for heat-pump, insulation, and whole-home retrofit contractors working under Czyste Powietrze. The system would read invoices, payment proofs, device cards, before-and-after energy documents, acceptance protocols, and photos; flag missing identifiers or version mismatches; and export a beneficiary-owned audit dossier. The wedge is not grant advice but fewer delayed payments and fewer contractor callbacks, initially validated in Wielkopolska through the family business and local energy auditors.
title: Clean-Air Payment Pack for Small Polish Retrofit Contractors
uncertainties: Frequency, causes, and monetary impact of payment-pack corrections by contractor segment.
Whether WFOŚiGW practices differ enough by region to require expensive manual maintenance.
Whether the program remains stable and funded long enough to support a standalone company.
